user_query: I need an object detection model to locate people, dogs, and cats in indoor and outdoor photographs. The objects may appear at different scales, under varied lighting, and may be partially occluded by furniture or other people. The model will run locally on a MacBook Air with an Apple M4 chip and 16 GB of unified memory, using Metal acceleration where supported. It should aim for a mAP@0.5:0.95 of approximately 0.40 or higher and recall of at least 0.75 for each class. Processing an image within roughly 500 milliseconds would be desirable.
use_case_description: Object detection to locate person, dog, cat in indoor and outdoor photographs.

available_hardware.details: Apple Silicon MacBook Air; Metal acceleration available; 16 GB unified memory.

dataset_selection_decision_evidence.rationale: Selection strategy: use a single coherent training family (Open Images 2019 detection train) as the primary pool to maximize a shared backbone across all three target classes (person, dog, cat) and to align with general photography domain. Open Images provides very large per-class training pools and consistent detection annotations, enabling efficient sampling and stable training on a MacBook Air with Metal acceleration. Per-class allocations are set to 2,000 images, aiming for roughly 2k total per class (6k total training images across all classes in the patch) to meet the Medium accuracy/latency target without overfitting or excessive training time. This preserves the rule of selecting only from exact dataset IDs listed under each class (Open Images train) and uses the primary pool for all three classes, keeping class-pool ratios balanced (2k/2k/2k). The approach leverages the large, diverse Open Images coverage across indoor/outdoor scenes typical of photography workloads, and it leaves room to enrich with additional families (e.g., LVIS or COCO) later if higher recall or long-tail coverage is desired. Estimated final per-class pool size is ~2,000 images (training), with the total selected training pool around 6,000 images before validation/test splits; actual final splits will be determined by deterministic code. The default download budget appears modest relative to the available data and was not a limiting factor for this selection.
